title: The Sun as Likeness of the First Greatness: Sevenfold Goods of Light Against the Seven Wickednesses of Night
arc: The teaching opens with the question of how the sun and moon were fashioned to the likeness of the First Greatness, and answers by enumerating seven goods which the luminary — as the visible icon of the Father — performs in the cosmos, then turns to set against them the seven corresponding wickednesses which night works when that light is withdrawn.
reading:
The chapter is built upon a single correspondential premise: the sun (with the moon beside it) is fashioned as the **likeness** of the First Greatness — the visible icon, in the cosmos, of the Father in his inmost Divine. This is why the opening calls him "the gate of Life and the stronghold of Peace, unto the great Aeon": the luminary is not merely an astronomical body but the doorway through which the Father's life shines into the natural, and the fortified place by which the Father's peace is held against the disturbance of night. Once this is established, the teaching simply unfolds what such an icon does — sevenfold, because seven is the fullness of holy work in ultimates — and then sets against it the equal-and-opposite sevenfold work of night.

The seven goods of the luminary trace a complete descent of Divine Truth through the discrete degrees of natural life. **First**, his light enters the eyes of all men: this is the illumination of the understanding, the banishing of the blindness that night had laid upon the intellect, so that men "walk in him" — that is, conduct their natural life within the medium of truth. **Second**, his coming brings rest and peace and bears away the fear and disturbance with which the heart had been filled all through the night: this is the quieting of the will, for once the understanding is illumined the affections are no longer thrown into turmoil by what they cannot see. **Third** is his vigilance: sleepers rise and awake, and those who had been compelled to keep armed watch before their encampments lay down that fearful vigil — this is the regenerative awakening of the soul from spiritual sleep, and the dismissing of the anxious self-defence which the natural man maintains in darkness.

The middle three goods describe the luminary's effect upon the lower natural. **Fourth**, he nourishes and gives might and taste and fragrance to the trees, fruits, crops, vegetables, flowers and grass of the earth: spiritually, the influx of Divine Truth feeds the perceptions (trees), brings forth works of life (fruits), and lends the savor and fragrance of divine love through the whole growth of the natural mind. **Fifth**, when he shines, the evil creeping things and the predatory wild beasts that are full of evil are driven into their dens: the corrupt and predatory affections of the natural cannot operate in the open under the light of truth, but are restrained into their proper confinement. **Sixth**, his light heals the plague of men and dissolves the evil magics of wicked men: this is the purification of the natural from falsity-from-evil, the dissolving of those false operations by which the proprium binds and afflicts the soul.

The **seventh** good is the consummating one and the key to the whole sequence: he is manifested forth and reveals from the cosmos "the sign of the Radiance of the aeons of Light from which he came forth — to be their sign in this cosmos, so that the entire creation may see." The sun is not its own source. It is a sign, an icon, set in the firmament so that all creation may know there is a Land of Light from which this radiance proceeds. This seventh good is therefore the very purpose of the first six: every previous operation — illumination, peace, awakening, nourishment, restraint of evil, purification — exists so that creation may finally read in the visible sun the invisible Father, and trace the likeness back to the First Greatness it was fashioned to express.

Against this completed sevenfold work, the teaching then begins (and the surviving text breaks off after the first item) the parallel sevenfold work of **night**. Night, for the lexicon of this corpus, is a state of falsity covering truth, and the surviving first wickedness states the principle exactly: when the sun sets and draws his rays back into himself, the shadow of night spreads over the whole cosmos, the eyes of men are filled with darkness, and they cannot see forth nor discern. This is the precise inversion of the first good: where light entered the eyes and abolished blindness, night refills the eyes with darkness and abolishes discrimination. The reader is meant to understand that the remaining six wickednesses of night will likewise undo, point for point, the six remaining goods of the sun — disturbance instead of peace, sleep and fearful watch instead of awakening, withering instead of nourishment, the prowling of beasts instead of their confinement, plague and magic instead of healing, and concealment of the sign of the Father's Radiance instead of its revelation.

The whole teaching is therefore a contemplation of why the sun is what it is. Because it is the likeness of the First Greatness, every operation it performs in the natural is a correspondence of what Divine Truth in its illuminating manifestation does in the soul; and because night is the contrary state of falsity, every operation of night is a correspondence of what falsity-from-evil does when the Lord's truth is withdrawn from a state. The sevenfold structure on each side is not a list but a complete cycle: the full work of Light in ultimates, opposed by the full counter-work of Darkness, with the luminary itself standing as the gate and stronghold by which the cosmos is kept in conjunction with the Father.
